title: Count Subsets With Sum
statement: Count the subsets of `nums` whose values add up to `target`. The empty subset sums to 0. Values are non-negative and the list has at most 20 elements, so meet-in-the-middle splits the list in half, enumerates both halves, and counts complementary sums.
hints: Count how often each sum appears on the right half.
Every left sum needs the right sum target - left. Add those frequencies.

approaches.name: Full recursion
approaches.explanation: Fine as an oracle when n is small.

approaches.name: Meet in the middle
approaches.explanation: The classic split for n around 40, and already useful at 20.

editorial: Split the array at the midpoint. Build every subset sum of each half by extending a list: for each existing sum, append that sum plus the new element. A counter on the right half answers, for each left sum, how many subsets complete the target. The product of the half sizes is far smaller than 2^n once n grows, and the count includes every subset exactly once because every subset has a unique split across the midpoint.

examples.explanation: Only the empty subset sums to 0.
